detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

When `/v1/completions` truncates a text prompt with an explicit `truncation_side`, `echo=true` still returns the original text. This change updates the echoed text to match the tokens sent to the engine, following up on #61876.

## Claims

The fix applies to streaming and non-streaming responses. Requests whose tokens are unchanged keep their original text. Requests that do not need prompt detokenization do not perform an additional decode.

## Validation

With `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` served as `qwen`:

The role labels below are plain text in the completion prompt.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen",
       "prompt":"Role: You are a helpful geography assistant. Answer in one sentence.\nUser: What is the capital of France?\nAssistant:",
       "echo":true,"truncate_prompt_tokens":12,"truncation_side":"left"}'
```

The prompt has 27 tokens and is truncated to 12. Compare the echoed prefix of `choices[0].text`, omitting the generated continuation. Before the fix, it still includes the discarded system-style instruction:

```text
Role: You are a helpful geography assistant. Answer in one sentence.
User: What is the capital of France?
Assistant:
```

After the fix, the echoed prefix contains only the retained user question and assistant label:

```text
User: What is the capital of France?
Assistant:
```

Both versions report 12 prompt tokens. Generation uses the request defaults; no logprobs are requested.

The request was tested three times before and after the initial fix. All three responses included the discarded instruction before the fix and only the retained prompt after it. Only the echoed prefix was compared; the generated continuation is not part of this check.

The regression tests reproduce the added BOS echo with the original tokenization path, and an HTTP 500 / streaming error for a BOS-only prefix without the empty-text fix. All six regression cases now pass.

Current validation:

- 95 renderer, preprocessing, text-offset and API utility tests passed.
- 8 OPT HTTP tests passed: six streaming/non-streaming regression cases and two existing completion tests. Echoed text is checked against the retained user content plus the matching `echo=false` generation.
- All applicable pre-commit checks, including mypy, passed.

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_completions.py \
  tests/renderers/inputs/test_preprocess.py \
  tests/renderers/test_token_offsets.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py -q
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -q \
  -k 'truncated_echo_excludes_only_added_special_tokens or test_completion_truncation_side_controls_prompt_truncation or test_single_completion'
pre-commit run --files vllm/inputs/llm.py vllm/renderers/base.py \
  vllm/renderers/params.py vllm/tokenizers/protocol.py vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py \
  tests/renderers/test_completions.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py \
  docs/serving/online_serving/openai_compatible_server.md
```

## Details

Post-tokenization validation truncates the token IDs but leaves the original `prompt` string in place. The detokenization added by #61876 is skipped because that string is still present. `BaseRenderer` now also detokenizes when validation replaces the token sequence, rebuilding the text from the retained tokens in both synchronous and asynchronous paths.

For text prompts, an encoding-time `special_tokens_mask` distinguishes automatically added tokens from special tokens in the user's text. The mask follows truncation and is consumed when rebuilding text, without changing the model input IDs. Empty echoed prefixes are preserved when creating engine inputs.

This covers truncation during post-tokenization validation, not truncation performed inside the tokenizer.

This is separate from #61876, which fixes detokenization order for token-ID inputs, and #62684, which handles Rust echo with `return_token_ids=true`.

+class HfTokensPrompt(TokensPrompt, total=False):
+    """Tokenized HF prompt with metadata for rebuilding echoed text."""
+
+    prompt_special_tokens_mask: list[int]
+    """Mask for tokens retained by truncation, before any padding."""
+
+
+def tokenize_prompt(
+    tokenizer: TokenizerLike,
+    prompt: TextPrompt,
+    params: TokenizeParams,
+    *,
+    want_offsets: bool = False,
+) -> HfTokensPrompt:
+    """Tokenize text, preserving an optional mask for truncated echoes."""
+    # The mask identifies truncated text inputs even when no tokens were added.
+    want_special_tokens_mask = (
+        params.needs_detokenization
+        and params.truncate_prompt_tokens is not None
+        and params.truncation_side is not None
+    )
+    kwargs = params.get_encode_kwargs()
+    if want_offsets:
+        kwargs["return_offsets_mapping"] = True
+    if want_special_tokens_mask:
+        encoding = encode_with_special_tokens_mask(
+            tokenizer, prompt["prompt"], **kwargs
+        )
+    else:
+        encoding = tokenizer(prompt["prompt"], **kwargs)
+
+    tokenized = cast(
+        HfTokensPrompt,
+        BaseRenderer._build_tokens_prompt(
+            encoding["input_ids"],
+            prompt,
+            offset_mapping=encoding["offset_mapping"] if want_offsets else None,
+        ),
+    )
+    token_ids = tokenized["prompt_token_ids"]
+    if (
+        want_special_tokens_mask
+        and (mask := encoding.get("special_tokens_mask")) is not None
+        and len(mask) == len(token_ids)
+        and (truncation := params._truncation_slice(tokenizer, len(token_ids)))
+        is not None
+    ):
+        tokenized["prompt_special_tokens_mask"] = mask[truncation]
+    return tokenized

🟡 (optional) Completion clients using `echo=true` with `truncation_side="right"` on BOS-adding models (e.g. Llama) would get echoed text starting with a literal special token like `<|begin_of_text|>`. A text prompt's "prompt" is now rebuilt with `tokenizer.decode(prompt_token_ids)`, and `decode` defaults to `skip_special_tokens=False`. Right truncation keeps the BOS that `add_special_tokens` inserted. Fix: build the echo for text prompts from user content only, with no tokens the tokenizer added. Slice the original text using the retained tokens' offsets, or decode with special tokens skipped. Same change at the async path, base.py:740-745.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a POST to /v1/completions with a text prompt, `echo=true`, `truncate_prompt_tokens=N` and `truncation_side="right"`, on a tokenizer that adds BOS (`add_special_tokens` is True by default). get_encode_kwargs turns off tokenizer truncation in this case, so `_token_truncation` slices the list. The new identity check at base.py:694-697 then fires, and `_detokenize_prompt` (base.py:645-647) calls `tokenizer.decode(ids)` with `skip_special_tokens=False` (vllm/tokenizers/protocol.py:120-121). Because right truncation keeps index 0, the BOS stays and its text form is decoded into prompt["prompt"]. completion/serving.py:370 and :604 then return `prompt_text + output.text`, so the echo starts with `<|begin_of_text|>` (or `<s>`), text the user never sent. On the base branch the user's own text was echoed and no special-token strings appeared. The PR's validation used Qwen, which has no BOS, so it would not show this. Left truncation cuts the BOS off and is not affected.

**Verification:** _token_truncation returns a new list (params.py:516), so the check at base.py:694-697 fires. _detokenize_prompt (base.py:647) calls `tokenizer.decode(prompt["prompt_token_ids"])` with no skip_special_tokens argument. Result: the echoed text starts with a literal "<|begin_of_text|>" that the client never sent. The base kept the original text for text prompts.

</details>

In that case get_encode_kwargs passes `truncation=True, max_length` to the tokenizer. The tokenizer truncates, so post-tokenization returns the same list object and the `is not original_token_ids` check never fires. Fix: also rebuild the text when tokenizer-level truncation was active and actually shortened the prompt. For example, set a flag in the text branch when `truncate_prompt_tokens` is set and the token count reaches `max_length`, and apply it in the sync and async paths (base.py:740-744).
_A small fix can ride a push you are already making; otherwise a short reply is enough._

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: /v1/completions with a text prompt, `echo=true` and `truncate_prompt_tokens=12`, with no `truncation_side`. This is the default and most common way to truncate. vllm/renderers/params.py get_encode_kwargs only disables tokenizer truncation when `truncation_side is not None and truncate_prompt_tokens is not None`. Otherwise it returns `truncation=True, max_length=...`, so `_tokenize_prompt` already yields the truncated list. In `_validate_tokens`, `_token_truncation` sees `max_length >= len(tokens)` and returns the same object. As a result `prompt.get("prompt_token_ids") is not original_token_ids` is False at base.py:696, and since "prompt" is present no detokenization happens. completion/serving.py:604 echoes the full untruncated prompt while `usage.prompt_tokens` reports 12. The base branch behaves the same way, so the bug the PR title names ("Refresh echoed text after prompt truncation") stays open for default-side truncation. The PR description scopes this out, but it is the main truncation path.

**Verification:** Pre-existing. Trigger: a /v1/completions request with `echo=true` and `truncate_prompt_tokens` smaller than the prompt length, with `truncation_side` left unset. The echoed text is still the full original prompt, but the engine receives the truncated tokens. The check at base.py:694-697 (async copy at 741-744) skips detokenization, as the base code's condition did.

</details>

🟡 (optional) Deployments with a custom tokenizer may now get HTTP 500 on `echo=true` completions using `truncate_prompt_tokens` plus `truncation_side`; the base branch served them. The request path at base.py:677-697 calls `num_special_tokens_to_add()` and passes `return_special_tokens_mask=True`. It then reads `encoding["special_tokens_mask"]` with no capability check. Fix: make the mask best-effort, so a tokenizer that raises `NotImplementedError` or `TypeError`, or returns no mask key, falls back to unmasked decoding. Also skip the mask when its length differs from `input_ids`. HF and Mistral tokenizers keep their current behaviour.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger needs a tokenizer registered through `TokenizerRegistry.register` (vllm/tokenizers/registry.py:70) that does not implement the new contract. One kind inherits the `TokenizerLike` default `num_special_tokens_to_add`, which raises `NotImplementedError` (protocol.py:26-27). Another keeps the old fixed `__call__(text, text_pair, add_special_tokens, truncation, max_length)` signature. inline_comments.body:
🔴 Users of DeepSeek V3.2/V4, Kimi K3 and Inkling models still get a literal BOS such as `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` echoed after `truncation_side="right"` truncation. The base branch echoed only their own text. The mask-producing `_tokenize_prompt` override exists only in HfRenderer, MistralRenderer and CohereRenderer. Those other renderers subclass BaseRenderer directly, so the new identity check decodes the BOS with no mask. Fix: produce the mask for every renderer by moving this override into `BaseRenderer._tokenize_prompt`, keeping the TypeError/NotImplementedError fallback, which covers the 4 classes listed. Same gap at 4 sites (deepseek_v32.py:20, deepseek_v4.py:24, kimi_k3.py:143, inkling.py:91).

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a POST to /v1/completions on a DeepSeek V3.2 or V4 model. The request has a text prompt, `echo=true`, `truncate_prompt_tokens=N` and `truncation_side="right"`, with add_special_tokens left at its default of True. DeepseekV32Renderer (vllm/renderers/deepseek_v32.py:20) does not override `_tokenize_prompt`, so it runs the base version (base.py:667). Its tokenizer is an HF TokenizersBackend (vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v32.py:80), which prepends BOS. The base version never sets `prompt_special_tokens_mask`. `_token_truncation` returns a new list, so the new `is not original_token_ids` check at base.py:745/794 fires. `_get_detokenization_tokens` then finds no mask and decodes every ID, so the echo starts with the BOS string. On the base branch, text prompts kept their original text and no special-token string appeared. The cohere.py comment says the override was added there because that renderer "does not inherit HfRenderer". DeepseekV4Renderer, KimiK3Renderer and InklingRenderer are in the same position and were not covered.

**Verification:** deepseek_v32.py:20, deepseek_v4.py:24, kimi_k3.py:143 and inkling.py:91 use base.py:667 `_tokenize_prompt`, which never sets `prompt_special_tokens_mask`. Truncation does `tokens[truncation]` (params.py:517), so the new `is not original_token_ids` check forces `_detokenize_prompt`, and the BOS is decoded into the echoed text. On the base branch, the original text was echoed with no BOS literal.

</details>
